subject: Re: Tier blending credit reallocation — orderform exhibit redline
messages:
From: Maya Patterson <maya.p@acmehealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: acme-procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tier blending credits — request to move Year1 allocation into Yr2?

Diego / Marissa,

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. Our procurement team ran the numbers overnight and we have a follow-up request on the pricing exhibits. The core ask: can Acme shift up to 25% of the Year 1 committed credits in Exhibit C into Year 2 as a credit reallocation, so we can smooth cash flow this fiscal year?

Key constraints from our side: we need the reallocation to be explicit in the orderform (so our finance can book it), it must not expand the total committed volume (no net increase in spend), and our auditors want a clear floor/cap that prevents front-loading.

Please send a redline we can circulate — legal will want to review. Also flag any impact on the floor/cap calculations in Exhibit B if this reallocation is accepted. We were hoping to finalize procurement paperwork by end of next week.

Maya Patterson
Director, Strategic Procurement
Acme Health

Attachments: none
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patterson <maya.p@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tier blending credits — request to move Year1 allocation into Yr2?

Maya — thanks for the clear summary. Short answer: we can accommodate a limited reallocation but need tight guardrails to protect the pricing caps/floors and to avoid gaming of volume discounts.

I've attached an initial redline (redline_exhibit_C_v3.pdf) and the updated orderform schedule (orderform_schedule_v2.xlsx) that implements a 20% maximum reallocation from Year 1 to Year 2. Highlights:
- Reallocation limited to non-recurring promotional credits (so it can't be used to augment baseline committed volume).
- An explicit true-up at the end of Year 2 to reconcile unit pricing and any threshold triggers.
- Cap/floor adjustment: Exhibit B's effective floor will be calculated on post-reallocation committed volume; caps remain tied to total annual spend to avoid raising incremental discounts.

Tagging Laura for legal redline review and Karthik for any finance/recognition notes. If legal is comfortable, we can present the docs back to your procurement team tonight for signature routing.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive — Strategic
Redwood Inference

Attachments (stubs): redline_exhibit_C_v3.pdf (PDF, annotated), orderform_schedule_v2.xlsx (xlsx, delta cells highlighted)

Subject: RE: Tier blending credits — legal comments on Exhibit C redline

Diego / team,

Reviewed the redline. Overall acceptable with the caveats below — I've attached a clean set of legal comments (legal_comments_exhibit_C.docx) and an annotated PDF. Proposed edits:
1) Narrow the reallocation bucket: limit to promotional or one-time credits explicitly described in Section 3.2 (prevents reclassifying baseline committed units).
2) Add anti-stacking language: credits moved between years cannot be used to re-trigger staircase discounts that were satisfied in Year 1.
3) True-up mechanics: require a 60-day post-Year-2 reconciliation window and state that any reclaimed credits will be converted to a dollar-for-dollar credit against future invoices, not retroactive price adjustments.
4) Audit & reporting: Acme must provide a one-time supporting schedule showing how reallocated credits were applied; Redwood reserves the right to audit that schedule within 90 days.
5) Cap/floor formula clarification: Exhibit B, Appendix A — change the denominator to 'committed baseline volume' (post-reallocation) and preserve the original cap percentage calculation.

I recommend we present the redline to Acme with the 20% limit Diego proposed and the above legal edits. If procurement pushes for 25% we should ask for a short-term price hold (90 days) and an escrow credit mechanism to protect revenue.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments (stubs): legal_comments_exhibit_C.docx (Word, inline comments), redline_exhibit_C_v3_annotated.pdf (PDF)

Subject: Final — revised reallocation clause and next steps

Maya — thanks, and appreciate the speedy turnaround. Per Laura's comments we've incorporated the legal guardrails into Exhibit C and limited reallocation to 20% of Year 1 committed credits (promotional/non-recurring only). We've also clarified the Exhibit B cap/floor denominator and added the 60-day true-up and audit language.

Action items:
- Acme procurement to confirm acceptance of the attached redline (.pdf) and confirm whether you will sign the updated orderform or prefer DocuSign routing.
- Redwood finance (Karthik) will prepare a short recognition memo for Acme accounting to explain the Year 1→Year 2 shift for auditors.
- If Acme needs the 25% threshold instead of 20%, we can escalate for a temporary 90-day price hold and escrow credit mechanism — let us know ASAP.

Tentative timeline: sign by 2026-09-01 to meet your internal quarter close.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-min call to walk legal through the clauses if helpful.
